clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old postmenopausal female presented with right breast swelling, pain, and bloody nipple discharge. Initial imaging revealed a 7.5 cm retroareolar mass (BIRADS 4). A skin punch biopsy showed inflammatory changes, and incision and drainage yielded purulent fluid, leading to a diagnosis of breast abscess and clinical improvement with antibiotics. The patient was lost to follow-up but returned one year later with a new palpable mass, new nipple retraction, and persistent bloody nipple discharge. Repeat imaging showed a 4.0 cm irregular hypoechoic mass. An ultrasound-guided core biopsy of this mass confirmed a benign intraductal papilloma.
